tests/grok-lane.bats test 11 ("grok Use route is refused citing Setup when unauthenticated") is a host-environment-sensitive test defect, not a product defect, and it predates this plan. Isolation run 2026-07-31 under flock /tmp/foreman-bats.lock: pass=11 fail=0 baseline=11 delta=0, so it passes alone. In the full suite (/root/fm-logs/suite-a2.log line 204) it failed on [ "$status" -ne 0 ], meaning lane-run.sh exited 0 instead of refusing. Mechanism, reproduced directly: lane-run.sh sources $HOME/.foreman/env.sh, which prepends /root/.local/bin to the FRONT of PATH when that directory is absent. The suite ran under systemd-run, whose default PATH (/usr/local/sbin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/sbin:/usr/bin:/snap/bin) has no /root/.local/bin. The prepend therefore landed ahead of the test PATH shim, and the readiness gate probed the real authenticated /root/.local/bin/grok instead of the not-authenticated shim. Reproduction: env -i HOME=/root PATH=<systemd default> bash --noprofile --norc -c PATH=/tmp/fmshim:$PATH; . /root/.foreman/env.sh; command -v grok -> /root/.local/bin/grok. Under a login PATH the same command resolves /tmp/fmshim/grok, which is why it passes in isolation. Blame: env.sh sourcing is a0e809d (2026-07-30), the readiness gate is a432037 (2026-07-18); both predate every commit of this plan, and no commit of this plan touches lane-run.sh or the test file. Scope into a later plan: give the Use-path readiness gate a test seam so it cannot resolve real vendor CLIs, or make lane-run.sh append rather than prepend the env-file PATH.

tests/lifecycle-gate.bats test 1 ("Use refuses a not-ready grok lane at the door, citing Setup") has the same root cause as tests/grok-lane.bats test 11 and is the same host-environment-sensitive test defect, not a product defect. The readiness gate then probed the real authenticated grok, reported LANE_READY: grok=yes, and let the lane through. Blame a0e809d (2026-07-30) and a432037 (2026-07-18); both predate this plan, and no commit of this plan touches lane-run.sh or the test file. Fix it together with tests/grok-lane.bats test 11 in a later plan.

tests/vendor-isolation.bats test 7 ("lane-run (LANE_VENDOR=claude, fake launcher shim): CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR exported, normalized") is a host-environment-sensitive test defect, not a product defect, and it predates this plan. In the full suite (/root/fm-logs/suite-a2.log line 567) it failed on [ "$status" -eq 0 ] at tests/vendor-isolation.bats line 240, meaning lane-run.sh refused the lane. Mechanism: the test installs NO claude shim, so the Use-path readiness gate ran the real env/tool-check.sh --lane claude against the real host. On this host claude resolves only through an fnm multishell directory that the login profile creates. Reproduced: under the systemd-run PATH with a non-login shell, command -v claude returns nothing, so tool-check reports status=missing and LANE_READY: claude=no, and the gate exits EXIT_CONFIG. Under a login shell claude resolves and the test passes. The readiness gate is a432037 (2026-07-18); no commit of this plan touches lane-run.sh or the test file. Scope into a later plan: stub the claude probe, or make the gate injectable so no test depends on real host vendor authentication.
